writer_policy.input: Fresh RDKit MolFromSmiles input with atom indexing preserved; cases with atom_order renumber a fresh parse using Chem.RenumberAtoms
writer_policy.component_order: RDKit constructs fragments in input atom order and concatenates them in that order when canonical is false.

completeness_basis.argument: For these fixed parsed graphs and writer parameters, RDKit's noncanonical traversal emits one depth-first walk per selected component root. At each atom it emits one continuation child and renders each other unvisited child as a branch, so the finite root and child-order cases listed per input contain every possible traversal. Ring closure numbering is deterministic and introduces no additional ordering choice here. Each listed upper-bound traversal has a replayed MolToRandomSmilesVect witness, so the finite bound is attained and equals support. Each renumbered CC.O case has an ethane component with one distinct serialization and a singleton oxygen component with one spelling; the deterministic component construction and fixed noncanonical assembly therefore leave one output for that input atom order.

source_claims.claim: RDKit's first traversal selects the first depth-first walk and detects ring closures; its second traversal chooses a continuation child, emits remaining children as branches, and orders them according to the active random writer mode.

These lines define the fixed C/O and single-bond spellings, label ring closures from the first available integer, choose a random root when rootedAtAtom is -1, concatenate noncanonical fragments in constructed order, and seed random output generation for each witness call.
RDKit constructs connected fragments and preserves the source atom mapping used by noncanonical fragment concatenation.

completeness_basis.witnesses: Each case stores one positive replay seed per expected_support entry in index order. The cases were observed through fresh-molecule MolToRandomSmilesVect calls and replayed exactly. These observations establish membership; the source-derived upper bound establishes completeness.

cases.source: Fixed-input RDKit writer regime with complete support established by the pinned source-bounded root and child-order enumeration.
bound_cases: Either terminal root forces one orientation, yielding CCO or OCC.
The central root has two child orders, yielding C(C)O or C(O)C.

cases.source: Fixed-input RDKit writer regime with complete support established by the pinned source-bounded root and child-order enumeration.
bound_cases: The tertiary carbon root has three distinct child orders because its two carbon children are identical.
Either of the two equivalent methyl roots allows two orders for the remaining carbon and oxygen children at the tertiary carbon.
The oxygen root has one distinct order for the two equivalent carbon children at the tertiary carbon.
